svg.aria-label: Eighty-two paper slips, one for each semicolon and colon from English-original 1700s prose in a random sample of 100. Each turns over to pink if the mark glues two clauses that could each stand as a sentence, or dark if it separates a list, introduces a quotation, or sits in a heading or footnote. 36 of 50 semicolons glue two clauses (72%), and 19 of 32 colons do (59%).
